name: Valkyrie
summary: Broad swept wings with wingtip fins and elevators. It floats slowly and stays up a long time.
author: Kyle Boyer

sources.title: The POWERUP Paper Airplane Book, pp. 37–39 (photos from the requester)
sources.note: Folding order, measurements and diagrams for every step, and the finished shape

assumptions: The recipe starts from US Letter with 2.5 cm (1 in) cut off the top: 21.6 × 25.4 cm.
Step 3: "about 1¼ in from the top" is read as the crease sitting 3.2 cm below the tip.
Step 5: the fold line is 2.5 cm (1 in) below the top edge of the outward-folded flaps, as the diagram marks it.

Steps 6–7: the book calls this a swivel fold. Its result, a straight slant from the top edge down the side, is folded here as an inside reverse fold of the pocket corner along the first corner crease.
Step 9: "the outer edges" are read as the sheet's straight side edges, folded onto the diagonal creases. This matches the steep sides in the book's next diagram.

Steps 10–11: the app folds each side along its diagonal crease but doesn't show the small flap being tucked under the middle section. The photos don't make clear which flap it is. The step text keeps the book's instruction.

Steps 14 and 16: the wings fold on a line from the nose tip to 2.5 cm (1 in) from the bottom fold at the back. The book marks 1 in at the back; the pointed nose and slanted back edge in its diagram 19 fit a line from the tip.
Steps 17 and 19: the fins are about 1.3 cm wide at the back, widening to about 2.5 cm at the front, with the crease parallel to the wing's fold. The book shows the line but no measurement.
Steps 20–21: two 1.5 cm slits, 1.8 cm apart, cut square to the back edge between the fin and the body, with the tab bent up 20° in flight as in the book's photo. The book gives no measurements.

steps.title: Crease the middle
steps.text: Start with US Letter trimmed to 21.6 × 25.4 cm (cut 2.5 cm, 1 in, off the top). Fold it in half the long way, crease, and open it again.

steps.title: Fold the top corners in
steps.text: Bring each top corner down to the center crease to make a point.

steps.title: Crease the point
steps.text: Fold the tip straight down so the crease sits about 3.2 cm (1¼ in) below it. Crease well and open it again.

steps.title: Fold the inner edges out
steps.text: On each flap, fold the edge that lies along the center out to the side so it lands on the crease you just made. The flap corners will stick out past the sides of the point.

steps.title: Fold the top down
steps.text: Fold the whole top section down on a line 2.5 cm (1 in) below the top edge of the flaps you just folded out.

steps.title: Reverse fold the right corner
steps.text: At the top right, the flap's corner forms a little pocket. Open it slightly and push the corner down inside, between its two layers, so the side runs in one straight slant from the top edge.

steps.title: Reverse fold the left corner
steps.text: Do the same on the left: open the pocket and push the corner in between its layers.

steps.title: Crease the top corners
steps.text: Fold each top corner down to the center crease, so the top edge lies along it. Crease well and open them again.

steps.title: Fold the sides in
steps.text: Fold each straight side edge in so it lands on the diagonal crease you just made. The fold starts where that crease meets the side.

steps.title: Fold the right side in
steps.text: Fold the right side in along its diagonal crease. As it goes over, tuck the small flap at the top under the folded-down section in the middle; this locks the layers together.

steps.title: Fold the left side in
steps.text: Same on the left: fold along the diagonal crease and tuck the small top flap under the middle section.

steps.title: Turn it over
steps.text: Flip the paper so the folds face down.

steps.title: Fold in half
steps.text: Fold it in half along the center crease, so the folds end up on the outside.

steps.title: Fold the first wing
steps.text: Fold the top layer over on a line from the nose tip to a point 2.5 cm (1 in) from the bottom fold at the back.

steps.title: Turn it over
steps.text: Flip the plane so the other side faces up.

steps.title: Fold the second wing
steps.text: Same fold on this side: from the nose tip to 2.5 cm (1 in) from the bottom fold at the back. Line it up with the first wing.

steps.title: Fold the first fin
steps.text: Fold the outer edge of the top wing up to make a fin, about 1.3 cm wide at the back and widening to about 2.5 cm at the front. Keep the crease parallel to the wing's long folded edge.

steps.title: Turn it over
steps.text: Flip the plane so the other wing faces up.

steps.title: Fold the second fin
steps.text: Fold a matching fin on this wing, the same width as the first.

steps.title: Cut the elevators
steps.text: Hold the wings together, edges lined up. Cut two slits 1.5 cm (about ⅝ in) straight into the back edge, about 1.8 cm apart, between the fins and the body. Both wings get the same cuts.

steps.title: Open the wings
steps.text: Lift both wings until they're level, angled slightly up. Stand the fins upright and bend the elevator tabs up a little.

done.title: Ready to glide
done.text: Hold it under the wings and launch it gently and level. If the nose dives, bend the elevator tabs up a little more; if it climbs and stalls, bend them down.
